questions.question: Which of the following is a Buddhist text containing stories related to the previous births of the Buddha?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jatakas**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Jatakas** are a collection of stories in Buddhist literature that depict the previous births of **Buddha**. These stories are an integral part of Buddhist teachings and convey moral and philosophical lessons.
 
• The tales in the **Jatakas** are written in the form of narratives and contain moral teachings, ethical principles, and guidelines for righteous living. They often illustrate virtues like compassion, generosity, and wisdom.
 
• The stories are primarily in the form of prose and verse, making them accessible and relatable to the common people. *Hence, the correct answer is Jatakas.*
 
• The Jataka tales are considered significant in Buddhist philosophy because they provide insights into the Buddha's journey toward enlightenment across his previous lives.
 
• The tales are popular across various countries practicing **Buddhism**, such as India, Sri Lanka, Thailand, Myanmar, and Cambodia. These stories have been adapted into different art forms, including paintings, sculptures, and literature. *Hence, Jatakas are a crucial text in Buddhist tradition.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Characteristics of Jatakas:**

 
 
• **Jataka tales** consist of over 550 stories that narrate the previous incarnations of the Buddha. In each story, Buddha is depicted in various forms, such as animals, kings, or common individuals.
 
• The tales are compiled in the **Khuddaka Nikaya**, which is part of the **Sutta Pitaka** in Buddhist scriptures.
 
• These stories serve as a moral compass for individuals and provide lessons on virtues such as **compassion, honesty, and self-sacrifice.**
 
 
 
• **Other options explained:**
 
 
• **Panchatantra:** It is a collection of ancient Indian animal fables written by Vishnu Sharma to teach political and moral wisdom. It is not a Buddhist text.
 
• **Arthashastra:** Written by **Kautilya** (Chanakya), this text deals with statecraft, economics, and military strategy. It is also not related to Buddhism.
 
• **Manusmriti:** This is an ancient Hindu text that discusses laws, ethics, and the duties of individuals within society. It is unrelated to Buddhist teachings.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Historical Background:**

 
 
• The Jataka stories were composed between the **3rd century BCE** and the **5th century CE**. They are written in **Pali**, the canonical language of Theravada Buddhism.
 
• The Jataka tales are believed to have originated from oral traditions and later compiled into written texts.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Jataka Tales:**
 
 
• **The Monkey King:** A tale of a self-sacrificing monkey king who saves his troop by sacrificing himself.
 
• **The Golden Deer:** A story of the Buddha in the form of a golden deer, teaching the value of compassion and truth.
 
 
 
• **Significance:**
 
 
• The Jataka tales have influenced art, culture, and literature in Buddhist countries, including temple murals and storytelling traditions.
 
• They serve as an educational tool to spread Buddhist values and are still widely read and cherished today.

questions.question: The Visuddhimagga, a key Buddhist text, was written by which of the following scholars?
questions.solution: The correct answer is __**Buddhaghosa**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** __ • **The Visuddhimagga**, meaning "The Path of Purification," is a key text in **Buddhist literature**. It serves as an encyclopedic guide to the practice of Theravāda Buddhism. • This text was composed by the renowned scholar-monk **Buddhaghosa** in the **5th century CE**. *Hence, the correct answer is Buddhaghosa.* • **Buddhaghosa** was a commentator and translator who played a crucial role in systematizing and preserving the teachings of Theravāda Buddhism. His work is highly regarded in the Theravāda tradition. • The **Visuddhimagga** is divided into three main sections, corresponding to the threefold training in Buddhism: **Sīla (morality), Samādhi (concentration), and Paññā (wisdom).** • It provides detailed instructions on meditation, the interpretation of the Buddha's teachings, and the attainment of **nirvana**. • The text is based on the Pāli Canon, the foundational scripture of Theravāda Buddhism, and serves as a comprehensive manual for Buddhist practitioners. • The **Visuddhimagga** is highly influential and remains a cornerstone of Theravāda monastic education and spiritual practice. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** __ • **Buddhaghosa and His Contributions:** • **Buddhaghosa** was an Indian Theravāda Buddhist commentator who lived in the **5th century CE**. He is considered one of the most significant figures in the history of Theravāda Buddhism. • He traveled to **Sri Lanka**, where he studied the Pāli Canon and commentaries preserved in the Mahāvihāra monastery. • Buddhaghosa's primary goal was to systematize and translate the extensive Buddhist teachings from **Sinhalese** into **Pāli**, thereby preserving them for future generations. • **The Structure of Visuddhimagga:** • The text is divided into three sections: • **Sīla**: Focuses on ethical conduct and discipline for laypersons and monastics. • **Samādhi**: Explains meditation techniques, including the **jhana** states (levels of meditative absorption). • **Paññā**: Discusses wisdom, particularly insights into the nature of reality, impermanence, and the path to **nirvana**. • The text also includes commentaries on various aspects of the **Buddha's teachings**, making it an essential guide for practitioners and scholars. • **Key Features of the Visuddhimagga:** • The **Visuddhimagga** is considered a **practical guide** to meditation and ethical conduct, offering detailed instructions on achieving liberation. • It bridges the gap between the theoretical teachings of the **Pāli Canon** and their application in everyday practice. • The text is revered not only in **Sri Lanka** but also in other Theravāda Buddhist countries, such as **Thailand, Myanmar, and Cambodia.** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__** • **Contributions of Other Scholars:** • **Nagarjuna**: A key figure in Mahayana Buddhism, he is credited with founding the **Madhyamaka** school of thought, emphasizing the concept of **śūnyatā (emptiness).** • **Aryadeva**: A disciple of Nagarjuna, he expanded on the teachings of the Madhyamaka school and wrote influential texts such as **Four Hundred Verses.** • **Vasubandhu**: A prominent scholar in Mahayana Buddhism, he co-founded the **Yogacara** school and authored influential works like the **Abhidharmakośa.** • **Significance of the Visuddhimagga:** • The **Visuddhimagga** remains a cornerstone of Theravāda Buddhist practice and scholarship, providing a comprehensive framework for achieving spiritual liberation. • It is widely studied and respected in Buddhist monastic education systems across Theravāda countries. 6d:T3355,

questions.question:
Read the statements (A) and (R) and choose the appropriate option.

**Assertion (A): **Both Mahavira and Buddha laid emphasis on abandonment of homes in order to attain spiritual attainment.

**Reason (R):** They felt that only those who left their homes to stay at Sangha could gain true knowledge.

options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**both **____**(A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Both **Mahavira and Buddha** emphasized the **abandonment of homes** in order to attain** spiritual attainment.**
 
• This **assertion (A) is correct **as both **Mahavira,** the founder of Jainism, and **Buddha**, the founder of Buddhism, emphasized the **importance of renunciation** and leaving behind **worldly attachments** as part of their teachings.
 
• **Reason (R) provides an explanation for Assertion (A),** stating that they believed only those **who left their homes to stay at the Sangha** could **gain true knowledge.**
 
• The **Sangha** refers to the monastic community where individuals dedicated themselves to a life of spiritual practice and discipline.
 
• 
 
Both **Mahavira and Buddha** taught that by renouncing worldly life and joining the Sangha, individuals could detach themselves from desires, distractions, and attachments, thus creating the necessary conditions for spiritual growth and the attainment of true knowledge.

 

**​Therefore, both the assertion and the reason are true, and the reason correctly explains the assertion.**

questions.question: In Buddhist architecture the pinnacle rising from the top of the dome of a stupa is called _________.
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Yasti**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Yasti** is the pinnacle or spire that rises from the top of the dome of a **stupa** in **Buddhist architecture.**
 
• It symbolizes the **axis mundi**, or the connection between the earth and the heavens, reflecting the spiritual significance of the stupa.
 
• The **Yasti** is often topped with a **chhatri (umbrella)**, which represents protection and honor.
 
• It is a key component of stupa architecture, which serves as a sacred Buddhist structure for storing relics or commemorating the Buddha and his teachings.
 
• The stupa's architecture, including the **Yasti**, is designed to inspire meditation and spiritual reflection.
 
• The **Yasti**, along with other elements of the stupa, conveys symbolic meanings, including the Buddha's teachings and the path to enlightenment.
 
• Famous stupas such as the **Sanchi Stupa** and **Amaravati Stupa** feature the **Yasti** prominently in their design.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Andher**__

 __
 
• **Andher** is not a term associated with Buddhist architecture or stupa design.
 
• It may be a generic term or a name, but it does not relate to the pinnacle rising from the dome of a stupa.
 
 
 
• **Harmika**__
 __
 
• The **Harmika** is a small platform located at the top of the dome of the stupa, below the **Yasti**.
 
• It is typically square-shaped and represents the sacred abode of the gods.
 
• The **Harmika** is an important architectural feature in stupas, but it is distinct from the **Yasti**, which rises above it.
 
 
 
• **Medhi**__
 
 
• The **Medhi** refers to the circular terrace or platform surrounding the stupa's dome.
 
• It is often used as a path for **pradakshina (circumambulation)**, an important ritual in Buddhist practice.
 
• While it is a significant part of stupa architecture, it is not the pinnacle rising from the dome.

questions.question: Who among the following became a follower of Jainism towards the end of his life?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Chandragupta Maurya'**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__**Chandragupta Maurya**__

__
 
• Chandragupta Maurya (born: 345 BC, Ruled 321-297 BC]) was the** great emperor** of India.
 
• He founded the** Maurya Empire**.
 
• Chandragupta was successful in bringing the whole of India under one empire.
 
• Chandragupta Maurya was intelligent from his youth, he had all the qualities of a successful true ruler, which **Chanakya** recognized and gave him **political and social education**.
 
• Chandragupta Maurya **defeated Alexander **by following the **Chanakya policy**.
 
• When Chandragupta Maurya was** 50 **years old, he was inclined toward **Jainism**, his guru was also from Jainism whose name was **Bhadrabahu**.
 
• **He became a follower of Jainism towards the end of his life.**
 
• In 298 BCE, he gave his kingdom to his **son Bindusara** and went to Karnataka, where he meditated for 5 weeks without eating and drinking, which is called **Santhara**.
 
• This is how Chandragupta Maurya gave up his life.

Thus, the correct answer is Chandragupta Maurya__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9074044cf96dc1d09ca89eac99180c3d7440ade1b364d09d47931959bf693cc8.png] **__Confusion Points__** Ashoka followed Buddhism while Chandragupta Maurya followed Jainism.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements

1. Buddhist text Anguttar Nikaya mentioned about 16 Mahajanapadas.

2. Jainism text Bhagvati sutra mentioned about 16 Mahajanapadas.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Both 1 and 2__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• During the 6th century B.C **16 Mahajanapadas** existed.
 
• Buddhist text Anguttar Nikaya and Jainism text Bhagwati sutra mentioned Mahajanapada.
 
• The Anguttar Nikaya mentioned sixteen great nations in several places.
 
• The Bhagwati sutra mentioned the countries of Madhydesa, far east and south only.

questions.question: Which Gumpha at Khandagiri in Odisha, India is known for carvings of twenty-four Jain Teerthankars?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Trushula Gumpha**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Trushula Gumpha** at Khandagiri in Odisha is renowned for its intricate carvings of **twenty-four Jain Teerthankars**.
 
• The carvings depict the Jain Teerthankars in meditative poses, showcasing a deep connection to **Jain spirituality and philosophy.**
 
• Khandagiri and Udayagiri caves are significant archaeological sites that date back to the reign of King **Kharavela** of the Mahameghavahana dynasty.
 
• Trushula Gumpha stands out for its **artistic and religious importance**, reflecting the influence of Jainism in ancient Odisha.
 
• The caves are located near Bhubaneswar and are visited for their **historical, architectural, and religious significance.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jain Teerthankars:**

 
 
• The Teerthankars are revered spiritual teachers in Jainism who have attained liberation and enlightenment.
 
• There are twenty-four Jain Teerthankars, with Lord Mahavira being the last and most significant.
 
 
 
• **Khandagiri and Udayagiri Caves:**
 
 
• These caves are part of a historical site that represents Jain rock-cut architecture.
 
• They were carved during the reign of King Kharavela in the 1st century BCE.
 
• The site consists of numerous caves with inscriptions and carvings depicting Jain teachings and practices.
 
 
 
• **King Kharavela:**
 
 
• He was a ruler of the Mahameghavahana dynasty in ancient Odisha.
 
• Kharavela is known for his patronage of Jainism and contributions to art and architecture.
 
• The famous Hathi Gumpha inscription provides insights into his reign and achievements.
 
 
 
• **Jain Rock-Cut Architecture:**
 
 
• It involves carving sanctuaries, temples, and monasteries into natural rock formations.
 
• The architecture is marked by simplicity, reflecting Jain principles of non-attachment and minimalism.

questions.question: Which of the following is one of the 'three gems' (triratna) of Jainism?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Samyag-darshana**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The 'Three Gems' (Triratna) of Jainism are **Samyag-darshana (Right Faith), Samyag-jnana (Right Knowledge), and Samyag-charitra (Right Conduct).**
 
• **Samyag-darshana** refers to the right perception or faith, which involves realizing the truth about the soul and the universe.
 
• It is considered the foundational step in the path of liberation (Moksha) in Jain philosophy.
 
• The Triratna serves as a guide for ethical and spiritual development, emphasizing a life of non-violence (Ahimsa) and self-discipline.
 
• The ultimate goal of following the Triratna is to attain liberation from the cycle of birth and death (Samsara).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Samyag-jnana (Right Knowledge):**

 
 
• It refers to the correct understanding of the nature of reality, which includes the principles of Jain philosophy such as the concepts of Jiva (soul) and Ajiva (non-soul).
 
• Right Knowledge is free from doubts and delusions and is achieved through study and meditation.
 
 
 
• **Samyag-charitra (Right Conduct):**
 
 
• Right Conduct involves living a life of non-violence, truthfulness, celibacy, non-stealing, and non-possessiveness.
 
• It is the practical application of Right Faith and Right Knowledge in daily life.
 
 
 
• **Ahimsa (Non-violence):**
 
 
• Ahimsa is the central tenet of Jainism, emphasizing non-violence towards all living beings.
 
• It is closely linked to the practice of Right Conduct and is a key virtue in Jain philosophy.
 
 
 
• **Moksha (Liberation):**
 
 
• The ultimate goal of Jainism is Moksha, which is liberation from the cycle of birth and death (Samsara).
 
• It is achieved by following the path of the Triratna and practicing austerities to cleanse the soul of karmic impurities.

questions.question: ‘Ashta Mahasthana’ refers to the eight significant places associated with the life of the Buddha. Which among the following is NOT one of those?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Raigad.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ashta Mahasthana** associated with the life of the Buddha are :

 
 
• **Lumbini**
 
• **Bodh Gaya**
 
• **Sarnath**
 
• **Kushinagar**
 
• **Shravasti**
 
• **Sankissa**
 
• **Rajgriha**
 
• **Vaishali**
 
 
 
• **Gautama Buddha** was** born in** the **Lumbini village of Kapilavastu**,** Nepal in 563 B.C, ** in the **Shakya Kshatriya clan.​**​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Mahabhiniraskramana** or the Great Going Forth is **the event when Gautama Buddha left his home.**
 
• **Buddha visited Vaishali **and **learnt Sankhya darshan.**
 
• He went to** Rajgriha and learnt yoga**, **went to Uruvela** where he **attained enlightenment.**
 
• He went on to **Sarnath **where he** delivered his first sermon** also **called Dharmachakrapravartana.**
 
• He** died in 483 B.C** near** Kushinara** and the **event is known as Mahaparinirvana.**

questions.question:
Consider the following statements with respect to Jainism:

1. The practice of agriculture was considered sinful, according to Jainism.

2. The first Jain Council was convened at Pataliputra by the leader of the Digambaras.

Which of the following above given statements are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only 1**__.

**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__****

Mahavira rejected the authority of the Vedas and objected to the Vedic rituals.

__
 
• He advocated a very holy and ethical code of life.
 
• **Even the practice of agriculture was considered sinful** as it causes injury to the earth, worms and animals. **Hence statement 1 is correct**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/eaa43d31779ed0c64ea1245cc85003b624c6e9f55945d3e5d728ae048bda7401.png] 

 
• The first Jain Council was convened at Pataliputra by **Sthulabahu**, the **leader of the Shwetambars**.** Hence statement 2 is NOT correct**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Various Jain monks led by Bhadrabagu and Chandragupta Maurya went to Sravana Belgola in Karnataka.
 
• These came to be known as Digambars(Sky-clad or Naked).
 
• They follow the tenets of religion strictly.
 
• **The monks who stayed back in north India were led by Sthulbahu**, who changed the code of conduct for the monks.
 
• This sect became more liberal and started wearing white clothes. **Hence, they came to be known as Swetambars.**
